description: Committee recommends full cost recovery for EV charging.
User fees will be over $5 per hour, starting soon.
Also directs exploring private sector partnerships for charging.

chips.text: Defeated
2 for, 4 against
Mayor Block stated it is time to 'take the training wheels off' for EV charging subsidies.
Administration recommended a $3 per hour fee, but committee chose full cost recovery.
EV users appreciated the free pilot, but non-EV users complained about public funding.
Councillor Davies opposed subsidies, stating taxpayers should not fund private vehicle choices.
Public charging removes a key barrier for multi-unit residents without home options.
The pilot reduced an estimated 30 tons of greenhouse gases.
Administration will monitor EV charging station usage and report back in one year.

segments.title: Motion on EV charging program revenue
segments.takeaway: A motion was introduced and carried to direct net revenue from the EV charging program to the sustainable generation project.

segments.title: Presentation on EV charging station pilot
segments.takeaway: Administration presented the results of the EV charging station pilot, outlining usage patterns, costs, and five options for continuing the program, recommending a $3 per hour user fee.

segments.title: Committee questions and discussion
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned administration on monitoring usage, long-term funding, the rationale for recommended fees, and potential private sector partnerships.

segments.title: Debate on proposed user fees
segments.takeaway: Committee members debated the administration's recommended $3 per hour user fee versus a full cost recovery rate, with several expressing support for option 5.

segments.title: Vote on $3 per hour user fee (Option 4)
segments.takeaway: The committee voted against the administration's recommendation to implement a $3 per hour user fee for the EV charging stations.

segments.title: Vote on extending EV charging pilot
segments.takeaway: The committee voted against extending the EV charging pilot program with no user fees until December 31, 2025.

segments.title: Motion for full cost recovery user fee (Option 5)
segments.takeaway: Mayor Block moved a motion to implement a full cost recovery user fee of over $5 per hour for EV charging, starting as soon as possible.

segments.title: Vote on full cost recovery user fee
segments.takeaway: The committee voted to implement a full cost recovery user fee of over $5 per hour for EV charging, to start as soon as possible.

segments.title: Motion to explore private sector partnerships
segments.takeaway: A motion was introduced to direct administration to report back on a plan to engage the private sector in proliferating EV charging stations, considering cost-benefit for the city fleet and community.

segments.title: Vote on exploring private sector partnerships
segments.takeaway: The committee voted to direct administration to report back on a plan to engage the private sector in expanding EV charging stations, including a cost-benefit analysis for the city fleet and community

description: City will offer optional program for customers to offset electricity emissions.
Customers can buy renewable energy certificates from City projects.
This replaces the old Green Power program.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Staff noted the old program was oversubscribed but now has only 18 customers.
NULIFE GreenTech Inc. revenues would drop 20% without the program.
Mayor Block questioned why renewable energy costs more, disputing staff's explanation.
NULIFE GreenTech Inc. strongly urged adoption, citing economic benefits and local job creation.
Program helps the city meet its net zero GHG emissions target.
Mayor Block wants revenues to fund future renewable energy projects.

description: Allows six special events to extend noise hours in 2025, including Ribfest.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Organizers of six special events and nearby residents are affected.
Councillor Parker suggested staff research venue-specific noise complaints more thoroughly.
Saskatchewan Down Syndrome Society Movie in the Park is one approved event.

description: City Council acknowledged various information reports.

chips.text: Received as information
5 for, 0 against

description: Reports on $13.3 billion in water, wastewater, and stormwater assets.
Informs City Council's November budget deliberations.
Water user rates fund utilities; no current funding gaps.

chips.text: Recommended
Mayor Block clarified how water utility funding gaps are addressed.
Saskatoon residents pay water user rates to fund these utilities.
This is the first of new biennial asset management reports.
New water treatment plant construction is planned for 2026-2028.

description: City facilities and parks are aging and underfunded.
Proposed plan addresses funding gaps over five years.
Future report to detail funding options, including mill rate.

chips.text: Recommended
Staff noted shock at hearing other departments have no funding gaps.
Public services and community facilities are impacted by aging infrastructure.
Committee asked about costs for buildings not in the CBCM portfolio.
Sustainability and energy efficiency efforts are balanced with critical operational needs.
Staff will present funding options report to committee in September.

description: Saskatoon Light & Power assets are 9% in poor condition.
Underground cables in older neighborhoods cause increasing outages.
SLP faces $7.4 million funding gap for 2026 asset maintenance.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor appreciated receiving asset management reports early for better budget deliberation.
Residents in College Park, Erindale, Eastview, Westview, and Meadow Green face increasing outages.
SLP leveraged federal grants for LED streetlights and a new solar farm.
SLP will report on space needs and expansion options later this fall.

description: City avoids pesticides for pigeon control on its property.

description: Saskatoon will continue public education on boxelder bug prevention.
City will not remove trees to control boxelder bug infestations.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor asked if original motion mover was still on council.
Residents bothered by boxelder bugs will receive prevention information.
Tree removal conflicts with urban forest health and diversity goals.
Administration will issue annual public service announcements on boxelder bugs.
